examples.japanese: {本棚|ほんだな}に{本|ほん}を{並|なら}べた。
examples.english: I arranged books on the bookshelf.

examples.japanese: {本棚|ほんだな}がいっぱいになったので、{新|あたら}しいのを{買|か}った。
examples.english: The bookshelf got full, so I bought a new one.

examples.japanese: {本棚|ほんだな}を{見|み}れば、その{人|ひと}の{趣味|しゅみ}がわかる。
examples.english: You can tell someone's interests by looking at their bookshelf.

notes:
{本棚|ほんだな} is a compound of {本|ほん} (book) and {棚|たな} (shelf). It refers specifically to furniture for storing books.

Related terms:
- {書棚|しょだな} (more formal term for bookshelf)
- {書架|しょか} (library shelving)
- {棚|たな} (general shelf)

Common expressions:
- {本棚|ほんだな}を{整理|せいり}する (organize the bookshelf)
- {本棚|ほんだな}から{本|ほん}を{取|と}る (take a book from the shelf)
